cluster_summary: This cluster includes vulnerabilities where applications fail to enforce upper bounds on the size, count, or complexity of external input before performing memory or disk allocation, leading to resource exhaustion. The missing limits occur in various contexts: HTTP request/response body buffering, delimiter-split operations, numeric parameter validation, disk storage (cache, logs, downloads), type validation, size estimation, and parsing complexity.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 2 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Implement rotating file handlers with max size and backup count, LRU eviction for caches, and per-file/per-message byte and count caps for downloads..

sub_patterns.name: Missing resource capacity limits on persistent storage
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code writes to disk (log files, cache, downloaded media) without any capacity limit or eviction policy, allowing unbounded disk space consumption from repeated or large inputs.
